info.title: PropLine — Player Props & Sports Betting Odds API
info.description: Real-time player prop betting lines and game odds across 57 sports from 37 books — 23 sportsbooks (BetMGM, BetRivers, Betway, Bovada, Courtside, Sportzino, Heritage Sports, Jazz Sports, YouWager, Thrillzz, DraftKings, Fanatics, FanDuel, Fliff, Hard Rock Bet, Pinnacle, Unibet, 1xBet, TAB AU, ReBet, BetUS, BetOnline.ag, LowVig.ag), 6 DFS providers (PrizePicks, Underdog, Sleeper, Dabble, ParlayPlay, DraftKings Pick6), 3 prediction-market exchanges (Kalshi, Polymarket, Polymarket US), and 5 betting exchanges (Matchbook, Smarkets, Novig, ProphetX, SX Bet). Kalshi quotes more than game lines: NFL team totals (full game and 1st half), winning margin and half-time/full-time (NFL + NCAAF), NFL/MLB/WNBA player props, La Liga + EPL total and team corners, La Liga goalscorers, WTA 125 / ATP Challenger match winners, UFC fight goes the distance, and golf winner / make-cut / top 5, 10, 20 on the PGA and DP World Tours — filter with `bookmakers=kalshi`. Includes prop resolution against actual box-score stats, historical line movement with book-published timestamps, cross-book +EV with no-vig fair lines, an EV calculator for prices at books we don't carry, period-market filtering (?period=q1|h1|p1|f5|map1|s1|g1) on every odds endpoint, futures markets, and bulk CSV exports. Responses are the-odds-api compatible for drop-in migration. Every authenticated response carries live quota headers (X-Daily-Limit, X-Daily-Used, X-Daily-Remaining, X-Daily-Reset — unix seconds at the 00:00 UTC reset) so usage can be tracked programmatically without a dashboard. Standard rate-limit headers are sent alongside them (RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, RateLimit-Reset — seconds until reset — and RateLimit-Policy, plus the X-RateLimit-* spelling), so a generic client can self-throttle; quota headers ride every authenticated response including 4xx errors, but not a 401 for an invalid key; both 429 types carry Retry-After. Versioning is in the URL path and anything deprecated keeps serving for at least 12 months with RFC 8594 Deprecation and Sunset headers (https://prop-line.com/api-versioning).

parameters.description: Game-period filter. Omitted = full-game markets only (backwards-compat default). Pass canonical codes like 'q1', 'h1', 'p1', 'i6', 'f5', 'map1', 's1' (sets — tennis / volleyball), 'g1' (games — table tennis / badminton), comma-separated for multiple, or 'all' to include every period.

parameters.name: includeLinks
parameters.description: When true, adds a `link` field — the book's public event-page URL (plain navigation, no affiliate tagging) — per bookmaker block (odds endpoints) or per price row (/best-line). Links ship for Bovada, DraftKings, FanDuel, BetMGM, Kalshi, Polymarket, Smarkets, ProphetX and Novig; other books return null. Matches the-odds-api's includeLinks param. It also adds an `app_link` field (mobile app-open deep link; ProphetX only today, null elsewhere).

parameters.name: includeBookIds
parameters.description: When true, adds `book_event_id` per bookmaker block and `book_outcome_id` + `outcome_id` per outcome — each book's OWN identifiers for the event and the priced selection, plus PropLine's canonical outcome id (the value `line_movement` / `resolution` webhooks carry, so a delivery joins onto one REST row). Use these to join PropLine rows onto a book's native feed by id instead of matching on team names, players and lines. Kalshi ships both (event ticker + per-contract market ticker, e.g. KXMLBGAME-26AUG08NYYBOS-NYY); Bovada, DraftKings, FanDuel, BetMGM, Pinnacle, Polymarket, Smarkets, Novig, Matchbook, Sleeper, Dabble, ReBet, 1xBet, TAB AU and the Kambi books (BetRivers/Unibet) ship event ids. Books without a stable id return null. NB a two-sided market can share one book_outcome_id across both legs (a Kalshi contract is binary — Over/Under are its YES/NO sides); the outcome's `name` says which side. PropLine-specific, not a the-odds-api param.

parameters.name: includeDepth
parameters.description: When true, every outcome carries `depth`: the order-book levels BEYOND the served price, best-first, each {price, size} — American odds and the dollars a taker can spend at that level, at prices strictly worse than `price`. Up to 50 levels for Polymarket, Polymarket US and Kalshi (Kalshi: budgeted read, served only while under 3 minutes old and its top equals `price`), up to 3 for ProphetX; [] for every other book or an empty ladder. Omitted from the response unless set. PropLine-specific.

get.description:
Opening and closing line per (book, market, outcome).

Closing = the last snapshot at or before commence_time — the canonical line CLV-tracking tools measure against. Opening = the first snapshot we hold for the outcome, however far before kickoff the book posted it (use `opening_window` to limit the lookback). Returning both ends in one call is what makes this a complete CLV helper: on spreads and totals the point moves as much as the price (-3 -110 -> -3.5 -105), so `opening_point`/`point` matter as much as the prices.

Hobby+ gets full data; free tier is redacted (structure only). Same per-tier event-age cap as /odds/history.

get.description:
Compute cross-book +EV for a single event.

`markets` is an optional comma-separated filter. If omitted, every
market on the event is evaluated. Each market line that has Pinnacle
(preferred) or Bovada (fallback) coverage gets a no-vig fair price
and an EV% per book.

`bookmakers` is an optional comma-separated book-key filter — shop only the books you hold accounts at. It narrows the returned prices, never the anchor.

The anchor is chosen per line and always named: every line carries `fair_source`, and the response carries `fair_source_default` with the fallback order (pinnacle → polymarket → kalshi → bovada). One response routinely mixes several anchors, so read `fair_source` per line.

parameters.name: bookmakers
parameters.description: Comma-separated bookmaker keys (e.g. 'draftkings,fanduel'). Omitted = all books. Matches the-odds-api's bookmakers param. NB it narrows the PRICES only, never the fair-line anchor: bookmakers=draftkings still returns DraftKings EV% measured against Pinnacle. Lines where none of the requested books quote a price are omitted.

parameters.name: devig
parameters.description: How the anchor's vig is removed before the fair line is derived. 'multiplicative' (default) divides each implied probability by the booksum, spreading the overround evenly. 'shin' solves Shin's insider-trading model, which loads the overround onto the longshot side and corrects the favourite-longshot bias — negligible on a -110/-110 total, material on a +600 anytime scorer. The default is the only method the +EV backtest is measured on. Unknown values return 400.

parameters.name: fair_source
parameters.description: Fair-line anchor: one or more of pinnacle, polymarket, kalshi, bovada, smarkets (comma list = order tried), or 'consensus' alone (median no-vig across 3+ books with a clean, fresh market; books used are listed in fair_books). Anything else is 400.

parameters.name: max_age
parameters.description: Drop prices the book has not delivered within this many seconds (see each outcome's last_update). The fair line is unaffected.

get.description:
Cross-book best-line lookup for a single event.

For each (market, player, line) tuple on the event, returns the
single best American price across every comparable book PropLine
ingests, with the book name attached and an `all_prices` array
sorted best-first (one row per book, each with `last_update`) so
consumers can render runner-ups without a second request.

`markets` is an optional comma-separated filter (e.g.
`markets=h2h,spreads,pitcher_strikeouts`). When omitted, every
market on the event is included. `bookmakers` is an optional
comma-separated book-key filter (the-odds-api-compatible) — shop
only the books you hold accounts at.

DFS pick'em books (PrizePicks, Sleeper, Dabble, ParlayPlay, DraftKings Pick6) are excluded —
their quotes aren't independently bettable payouts; Underdog is
included only at its clean two-way lines (payout_multiplier ==
1.0). Companion to `/ev`: best-line tells you which book has the
highest payout right now; +EV tells you whether that price beats a
sharp no-vig fair line.

Hobby tier or higher sees prices. Free tier gets a redacted
teaser: the full structure — every line, side, book identity, and
the best-first ranking — with every price nulled, plus
`redacted: true` and an `upgrade_url`.

post.summary: Grade placed bets against the closing line (CLV)
post.description:
POST the bets you actually placed; each comes back with its closing line, the de-vigged closing fair probability, CLV, and the graded result once the game settles. Closing line value is the only durable proxy for whether a bettor has edge.

Stateless — nothing is stored.

Two CLV numbers are returned deliberately. `clv_pct` is price-vs-price: familiar and quotable, but vig-blind. `ev_vs_close_pct` scores your price against the DE-VIGGED close and is the honest one — a -110 taken into a -105/-115 close beat the price but not the fair line.

The de-vig uses the sharpest book quoting that line at close (Pinnacle first, then Polymarket / Kalshi / Bovada / Smarkets, falling back to your own book), reported as `fair_source`. De-vigging the book you bet at always returns a negative number because you paid its hold.

Matching is fail-closed: a bet that cannot be pinned to exactly one stored outcome returns `matched: false` with an `unmatched_reason` rather than a confident wrong match. Lines match by equality, never nearest-value.

Bets on events that have not started carry `closing_is_final: false` and are excluded from the summary averages. Max 500 bets per request.

Hobby+ gets full data; free tier is redacted (structure and match verdicts visible, every number nulled).

post.summary: Price a same-game parlay at the book's own correlated odds
post.description:
POST two to ten legs from ONE event and get back the book's own price for that exact slip — what a FanDuel customer would be offered for it at that moment, not a model of it. Beside it: `independent_price` (the product of the live single-leg prices) and `correlation_factor` (their ratio — the correlation the book is charging, below 1, or paying, above 1, for).

Book-native. `bookmaker` is `fanduel` (its own betslip pricer), `draftkings` (its SGP widget's pricer; legs are named by the nash selection id `?includeBookIds=true` serves, and `independent_price` is the product of our stored DK single prices) or `betonlineag` / `lowvig` (the Sportcast engine both Chico brands embed, same builder price); an unsupported value is a 422 `unsupported_bookmaker`. For the Chico books legs are matched against the book's own SGP board, wider than the game feed we store, so `independent_price` is null when a leg has no stored single price.

Legs are named exactly as `/odds` names them (market, name, description, point, period), so a leg is a copy-paste from an odds response; `book_outcome_id` from `?includeBookIds=true` is accepted as a shortcut.

Matching is fail-closed: a leg that does not pin to exactly one stored outcome is a 422 `leg_unmatched` naming the leg — an Over with no point on an event carrying two total lines is refused, not guessed. `quoted: false` means the book will not offer that combination as a same-game parlay; refused legs carry the book's own `failure_code`. 503 `book_unavailable` when the book's pricer does not answer. 422 `legs_not_at_book` when the book no longer recognises the `book_outcome_id`s sent — DraftKings re-issues its selection ids when an event goes in-play, so re-read them from `/odds?includeBookIds=true` rather than retrying the same slip.

`bookmaker=all` quotes every supported book on the same legs and returns `quotes` (one full single-book response per book that answered), `errors` (each book that could not price the slip, with the status + detail its own call would have returned) and `best_bookmaker` (the quoted book paying the most — the smallest correlation reduction on identical legs).

Every priced call is a live request to the book; quotes for an identical slip are shared for 15 seconds. Hobby+ gets the price; free tier gets the matched legs with every price nulled and never triggers a book call.

With `all` the response is `{quotes: [<one single-book response per book that answered>], errors: [{bookmaker, status, error, detail}], best_bookmaker}`; `best_bookmaker` is the quoted book paying the most, i.e. the one charging the smallest correlation reduction on these legs.

liquidity_updated_at.description: When the exchange last touched the resting order behind `liquidity` — the BOOK'S own timestamp, not our observation time. For ProphetX this is when ProphetX last placed or modified the order, not when we last read it (we re-read every rung each poll cycle; that read is `last_seen_at`): an untouched order keeps its original timestamp, so most rungs read old (measured 2026-09-25: median 67 minutes, p90 about 6 hours, 83% older than 20 minutes), and ProphetX does not continuously re-publish resting size, so an old order's amount can lag the book. Drop or discount sizes older than your own threshold. Null for books without resting size. On Polymarket / Polymarket US a timestamp with a null liquidity means the book was read at that time and had no resting ask on that side, so nothing was takeable at the served price.

liquidity.description: Dollars a bettor can actually stake at the quoted price. Exchange books publishing resting size (ProphetX, Novig (game lines every cycle; player props from its public order book, refreshed soonest game first; a null size with a non-null liquidity_updated_at means the book was read then and nothing backed the served price, null with null means not read yet), and — since 2026-09-22 — Kalshi, Polymarket and Polymarket US, where it is the top of book: contracts/shares resting at the best ask times that price; Polymarket US on game lines only, refreshed on a rotating budget, so read liquidity_updated_at) plus Pinnacle, where it is the book's posted max risk stake on the market (its own cap on what one bettor can risk at that price); null for every other book (including Smarkets and Matchbook: best back price only, no size), and for an exchange quote whose size the feed omitted. On a P2P exchange the best price is often a thin offer with only a few dollars behind it — filter or discount small values before treating the price as bettable. Refreshed every poll cycle independently of price movement. Exchange size changes never appear in /odds/history; a Pinnacle limit change does (its own snapshot row, price unchanged), and /odds/closing carries opening_liquidity beside liquidity. Neither fires line_movement webhooks. Pair with liquidity_updated_at: ProphetX does not continuously re-publish resting size, so a rung keeps its last-known amount until something happens to it (~27% of served rungs are more than 20 minutes stale).

suspended_at.description: Set when this book has taken the market off the board pregame (the pull-side twin of the market_suspended webhook). Null = on the board. The outcomes are then the last quoted legs, not a live price. Clears the moment the book delivers the market again.

line_type.description: milestone = an N+ threshold rung (outcome named "3+ Strikeouts", a per-threshold key like batter_2plus_hits, or a description naming the threshold such as "To Record 175+ Pass Yards"), Over/Under or Yes/No legs alike. Among one book's rows of a line market for one player or team (same key, period and team), exactly one is main: the book's own primary row where it labels one ("Spread" beside "Spread Alternate (...)", PrizePicks standard vs goblin/demon, ProphetX's own featured line), otherwise the most balanced pair (MLB/NHL full-game spreads prefer 1.5). Every other line is alternate; a group the book labels entirely alternate has no main. h2h, yes/no props, outrights and correct score are main. Where one row holds the main line for some players and an alternate for others (Kalshi / Polymarket US "Hits (line 0.5)" rows), each outcome also carries its own line_type.

liquidity.title: Liquidity
liquidity.description: Stake limit / resting size in force at this snapshot — the same field as the /odds outcome's liquidity, frozen per row. Pinnacle: its posted max risk stake; a Pinnacle limit change with NO price move is its own snapshot row (price/point repeat, this moves) and survives changes_only=true. Exchanges: the size at the moment of a price move only. Null for other books and on rows predating 2026-09-10.

outcome_id.title: Outcome Id
outcome_id.description: PropLine's stable id for this priced selection — the same value /odds?includeBookIds=true, /odds/closing, the resolved-props CSV and webhook payloads carry.

size.description: Dollars a taker can spend at this level.

name.title: Name
name.description: Which side this price is for. Player props come in three shapes: (1) two-way Over/Under: name is "Over"/"Under" (or "Yes"/"No"), player in description, line in point. (2) N+ milestone rung: name starts with a number and a plus ("3+ Total Bases"), player in description, point null; it is a YES bet on the player reaching N. (3) YES-only player list: name is the player (usually equal to description), point null; it is a YES bet at the threshold the market key states (batter_4plus_hits = 4+) or, for a plain key, 1+ ("to record a run", "to hit a home run"). Tell them apart by point (set = O/U), then a leading digit+'+' in name (rung), else the name is the player. Shapes 2 and 3 have no opposite leg.

description.title: Description
description.description: The subject the price belongs to: the player on player props (in all three shapes), the team on team totals/props, empty on plain game lines. On DFS books (PrizePicks, Underdog, Sleeper, Dabble, ParlayPlay) the tennis keys total_games / total_sets / total_tiebreaks name a player but settle on the WHOLE MATCH figure; each player's row is a separate pick on the same match number, so the two rows can carry different lines and prices. Sportsbooks quote the same keys once with an empty description.

price.title: Price
price.description: American odds. On DFS pick'em books this is not a bettable single: Dabble's two sides are its own zero-margin per-pick prices (the pair's implied probabilities sum to ~100%), which set that pick's share of an entry payout; Sleeper's is its per-pick payout multiplier; PrizePicks has no price and is shown at +100 on both sides. DFS pick'em books are excluded from /ev and /best-line.

point.title: Point
point.description: The line. On Bovada's both_teams_to_score_points ladder ("Both teams to score N or more points?", bare Yes/No legs) point carries the threshold N on both legs.

payout_multiplier.title: Payout Multiplier
payout_multiplier.description: DFS payout multiplier for boosted/discounted picks (Underdog Fantasy). Populated on EVERY Underdog outcome; null means the book is not Underdog. The quoted price ALREADY includes it: price is Underdog's own American price for the leg, so do not apply the multiplier again. It is Underdog's pick'em scaling relative to a standard pick (1.0): below 1 on the favoured side of a line, above 1 on the other. These are ordinary two-way prices and can be compared with sportsbook prices as-is; filtering to 1.0 drops about half of Underdog's board (/best-line and /ev currently use only the 1.0 lines).

dfs_odds_type.title: DFS Odds Type
dfs_odds_type.description: PrizePicks projection flavor: 'standard' (the true market line), 'goblin' (easier line / lower payout) or 'demon' (harder line / higher payout). Null for every traditional sportsbook. Filter to 'standard' to get PrizePicks's market line; goblin/demon are boosted/discounted alternates that each appear as their own per-line market. PrizePicks publishes no numeric multiplier for these, so only the flavor is surfaced.

last_change_at.title: Last Change At
last_change_at.description: PropLine's observed timestamp of the last time this outcome's price actually changed. Distinct from book_updated_at (the book's own publish-time, which only Bovada exposes): last_change_at is derived by PropLine and is populated for EVERY book, including Pinnacle and PrizePicks. We only advance it when price_american moves, so it is a true 'this line last changed at T' signal — compare it across books in one /odds call to detect repricing lag without a separate /odds/history call.

last_seen_at.title: Last Seen At
last_seen_at.description: The last delivery this outcome appeared in — the book still had it on the board at that poll, whether or not the price moved. For an outcome present in its market's latest delivery it equals the market's last_update; an older value means the book has stopped sending this selection while still sending the market (a withdrawal in progress — /odds withholds it entirely once that gap passes ~2 minutes, on every book; a briefly suspended in-play selection can therefore leave the response and come back). Consumer rule: a value older than the market's last_update means the selection missed the latest delivery — treat it as unavailable. last_change_at = when the price last moved; last_seen_at = when it was last offered. /odds only; null on rows predating 2026-08-26.

line_gap.title: Line Gap
line_gap.description: Signed line-difficulty delta for a PrizePicks goblin/demon outcome: point - the standard line for the same player+stat. Positive on a harder (demon) line, negative on an easier (goblin) line. Null when the outcome is not a PrizePicks goblin/demon, or when no standard line exists for that player+stat (PrizePicks often posts a player goblin/demon-only). PrizePicks publishes no numeric per-pick payout multiplier, so the flavor + this line gap are the modelable signals for fitting per-pick payout adjustments.

outcome_id.description: PropLine's own canonical id for this outcome row — the same value carried as `outcome_id` on `line_movement` and `resolution` webhook payloads, so a push delivery joins onto exactly one REST row with no name, side or line matching. Globally unique (one row per book/market/side; Over and Under are separate rows) and stable across price and point changes for the same (market, side, player). Books whose alt ladders put the line in the market description (PrizePicks goblin/demon, ProphetX, Fanatics, Marathon) get a NEW market — and a new id — when that line moves. Only set when the request passed includeBookIds=true.

book_outcome_id.description: This book's own identifier for the priced selection / contract (Kalshi: the per-contract market ticker; PrizePicks: the projection id used to build a populated entry URL; also Underdog, Sleeper, Dabble and Novig). Only set when the request passed includeBookIds=true. Whether the two legs of a market share one id varies by book — Kalshi and PrizePicks share it (`name` is the side), Underdog/Sleeper/Dabble/Novig give each leg its own — so group a pair by (market, player, point), not by id.

liquidity_updated_at.description: When the exchange last touched the resting order behind `liquidity` — the BOOK'S own timestamp, not our observation time. For ProphetX this is when ProphetX last placed or modified the order, not when we last read it (we re-read every rung each poll cycle; that read is `last_seen_at`): an untouched order keeps its original timestamp, so most rungs read old (measured 2026-09-25: median 67 minutes, p90 about 6 hours, 83% older than 20 minutes), and ProphetX does not continuously re-publish resting size, so an old order's amount can lag the book. Drop or discount sizes older than your own threshold. Kalshi's REST feed carries no book timestamp, so its value is the time on Kalshi's own push update that published exactly that price and size (MLB, NBA, NHL, WNBA, NFL, NCAAF, tennis), null until one has. Null for books without resting size. On Polymarket / Polymarket US a timestamp with a null liquidity means the book was read at that time and had no resting ask on that side, so nothing was takeable at the served price.

depth.description: Order-book levels BEYOND the served price, best-first — each {price: American odds, size: dollars a taker can spend at that level}. Up to 50 levels for Polymarket (asks beyond the best ask), Polymarket US (same rotating book read as liquidity) and Kalshi (budgeted order-book read, served only while under 3 minutes old and its top level equals price); up to 3 for ProphetX; [] for other books or an empty ladder. Refreshed with liquidity, never snapshotted. Present only when the request passed includeDepth=true.

liquidity.description: Dollars a bettor can actually stake at the quoted price. Exchange books publishing resting size (ProphetX, Novig (game lines every cycle; player props from its public order book, refreshed soonest game first; a null size with a non-null liquidity_updated_at means the book was read then and nothing backed the served price, null with null means not read yet), and — since 2026-09-22 — Kalshi, Polymarket and Polymarket US, where it is the top of book: contracts/shares resting at the best ask times that price; Polymarket US on every game line plus props for games in play or within 6 hours, refreshed on a rotating budget, so read liquidity_updated_at) plus Pinnacle, where it is the book's posted max risk stake on the market (its own cap on what one bettor can risk at that price); null for every other book (including Smarkets and Matchbook: best back price only, no size), and for an exchange quote whose size the feed omitted. On a P2P exchange the best price is often a thin offer with only a few dollars behind it — filter or discount small values before treating the price as bettable. Refreshed every poll cycle independently of price movement. Exchange size changes never appear in /odds/history; a Pinnacle limit change does (its own snapshot row, price unchanged), and /odds/closing carries opening_liquidity beside liquidity. Neither fires line_movement webhooks. Pair with liquidity_updated_at: ProphetX does not continuously re-publish resting size, so a rung keeps its last-known amount until something happens to it (~27% of served rungs are more than 20 minutes stale).

player_id.description: Stable, cross-referenceable league player id for joining the SAME player across books WITHOUT name matching — "{source}:{league_id}" (mlb:592450 = MLBAM person id, nba:/wnba: = CDN personId, nhl: = api-web playerId, espn:8439 = ESPN athlete id for soccer/NFL/NCAAF). Present only on player-prop markets; always null on game lines and futures. Null whenever we do not have a CONFIRMED, unambiguous id: a sport with no stable-id stats feed (tennis/golf/UFC/boxing/cricket/darts/esports/... — null forever), a player who has never graded, a book spelling that diverges from the league's (an extra surname / nickname — the id lands on the well-spelled book and stays null on the odd one), or a name two players share (ambiguous). We never guess an id: a missed join is safe, a wrong join is not. Unconditional (no query param). Coverage warms as games grade after launch.

side.description: Which side of the event a team-named leg is on: "home", "away" or "draw". Set on h2h and spread legs (and any market whose outcome name is one of the event's teams), resolved against home_team / away_team by the same rule that orders outcomes home-first. Use it when a market has only ONE leg (an exchange quoting only the side with a resting offer), which cannot be oriented by position. Null on Over/Under/Yes/No legs, player props, and any book spelling that matches neither team.

line_type.description: Per-outcome line_type. Present on every Kalshi and Polymarket US outcome, because those books ship one row per line carrying every player (e.g. "Hits (line 0.5)"), so one row can be main for some players and alternate for others. Omitted from the JSON on every other book.

is_main_line.title: Is Main Line
is_main_line.description: True on the line this book priced closest to even on both sides for the game, among lines that stood at kickoff; false on alternate-ladder rungs.

line_moved_in_play.title: Line Moved In Play
line_moved_in_play.description: True when the quote was re-priced after kickoff (an in-play line). Never marked main.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Stable league player id (e.g. mlb:677951); null when the name is unknown or shared by two players.

known_names.title: Known Names
known_names.description: Every normalized spelling graded under this id.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Stable league player id (e.g. mlb:677951); null when the name is unknown or shared by two players.

dfs_odds_type.title: DFS Odds Type
dfs_odds_type.description: Echo of the dfs_odds_type filter that scoped these trends (PrizePicks flavor: standard/goblin/demon). Null = cross-book, flavor-agnostic.

period.title: Period
period.description: Game period (q1, h1, f5, p1, s1, ...); null = full game. Same codes as /odds.

team.title: Team
team.description: On a totals market: the team a team total is scoped to; null for the game total. Same value as /odds.

outcome_id.title: Outcome Id
outcome_id.description: PropLine's stable id for this priced selection — the same value /odds?includeBookIds=true, /odds/history, /odds/closing, the resolved-props CSV and webhook payloads carry.

home_team_key.description: Stable per-team join key. Every bookmaker spelling of a club resolves to the same key ('St Mirren FC', 'St. Mirren' -> 'st_mirren'); a published key is never renamed. Null when the team cannot be identified with certainty (individual sports, small coverage tail) — fall back to the name.

home_team_id.description: The league's own permanent team id, namespaced by source ('mlb:147', 'espn.soccer:363', 'espn.nfl:12'). Use home_team_key to key data inside PropLine; use this to join against external datasets keyed on the same league ids. Sourced from the grading stats feeds, never guessed; null where unconfirmed.

home_team_logo_url.description: Public team logo image on the league's own CDN (ESPN's for NFL, college and soccer), built from home_team_id. Null exactly when home_team_id is null.

espn_event_id.description: ESPN's own id for the FIXTURE, kept from the match PropLine's live-scores loop already makes. Join on it to read score and clock straight from ESPN while taking odds from PropLine. Set for soccer and football; null for MLB, NBA, NHL and WNBA (their live scores come from each league's own API, whose ids are not ESPN's) and null for tennis.

mlb_game_pk.description: MLB Stats API gamePk for this game (MLB only; integer). We match each MLB event to at most one MLB game and each game to at most one event: same two teams and either the same start time, or the only game of that pair within 8 hours with no other event of ours near it. A matched event's commence_time is then set to MLB's own start time, so doubleheaders read correctly. Null when that is not certain: two candidate games, two of our events near one game, or a postponed or cancelled listing (MLB reuses a postponed game's gamePk for its makeup). A game MLB lists with a TBD start gets its gamePk but keeps our time. Use it to tell a doubleheader's two games apart.

tournament.description: Tennis only. The competition name as the first book to name it wrote it (e.g. "ATP Chengdu", "ITF M25 Pardubice") - a book's own spelling, not normalized. Set once, never changes. Null when no book named the competition, and on every other sport.

tour.description: Tennis only. Which tour the match belongs to - the single `tennis` sport key carries all of them. `Challenger` is the ATP Challenger Tour; WTA 125 events are `WTA`; `Team` = Davis Cup / Billie Jean King Cup / Laver Cup / United Cup. Doubles are not a separate tour (the tournament name says so). Set once, never changes. Null when no book named the competition, and on every other sport.

status.title: Status
status.description: One of upcoming, in_progress, final, postponed, cancelled, expired. `expired` means the event started 12h+ ago (6 days for golf, racing, cycling, cricket), no result feed has graded it, and no book has priced it in play for 2h or delivered any market for 30 min. Clients can close it out. It is derived at read time and is not a settlement: if a result arrives later the row reads `final`.

team_abbr.description: The box score's own team abbreviation for this player.

player_team.description: Null when the side cannot be identified, and always for individual sports (tennis, golf, UFC).

is_home.description: Null rather than guessed when the side is unidentifiable - a wrong home/away flag would corrupt every split built on it.

stats.description: Flat map of every stat_type recorded for this player in this game. Vocabulary is per-sport.
